method: Claude Code Agent-tool subagents in fresh scratch folders (deploy.sh for the skill arm, both arms told to load no other skill), 2 runs per arm, graded by blind judges per case against the rubric; fidelity from word-level SequenceMatcher on the edited file, new vocabulary, new quotes and protected strings. Not the CLI harness: routing is a proxy (one agent choosing from all 74 catalog descriptions), not observed skill loading.
fidelity_with: 0 additions by the judges in every skill run; similarity 0.87-1.00 except the cut-to-half case (0.68); protected strings 100% except one cut-to-half run per version rewording 'under the corner of the rug' to 'under its corner'
thresholds: set before the first run: better or same on every case and better on half; mean rubric with skill >= 0.80; zero additions; protected strings kept; similarity >= 0.90 proofread/copyedit and >= 0.60 otherwise; no prose on write-the-next-scene; routing correct on all
notes: q01 identical files both arms. q02 identical files; without-skill replies drafted replacement lines. q03 without swapped in its own wording. q04 without rewrote the scene, adding 7-10 details and a line of dialogue; with did a line edit and asked before moving the history paragraph. q05 without wrote 870-1040 word scenes inventing the reveal; with wrote nothing and asked for the writer's notes. q06 without added 'the dark was total' and other details. q07 (added at the owner's request for book context) both arms read chapters 1-2 unprompted and fixed the same things; the judge rated the skill runs 4 vs 5 for leaving two small echoes, so the context rule is not yet proven by this case. Version 1 (ec2a436a) measured all of q01-q06: with 0.98 mean rubric / 4.75 overall vs 0.72 / 3.25.
